example: the Jefferson era
傑佛森時代
a bygone (= past) era
過去的時代
the post-war era
戰後年代
They had worked for peace during the long era of conflict.
在漫長而衝突不斷的年代裡，他們努力爭取和平。
The fall of the Berlin wall marked the end of an era.
柏林圍牆的倒塌標記着一個時代的結束。

NONE: C2 to get rid of something completely or destroy something bad

example: The government claims to be doing all it can to eradicate corruption.
政府聲稱正盡其所能根治腐敗。
The disease that once claimed millions of lives has now been eradicated.
這種曾奪去數百萬人生命的疾病現在已被根除了。

T: B2 mainly US UK usually rub out to remove something, especially a pencil mark by rubbing it
抹去，擦掉（尤指鉛筆字跡）
› to remove recordings or information from a magnetic tape or disk
抹去（磁帶內容）；刪除（磁片裡的文件）
› to cause a feeling, memory, or period of time to be completely forgotten
（從頭腦中）清除，消除；忘卻（感覺、記憶等）
› literary to remove or destroy something, especially something that shows that that person or thing ever existed or happened

example: It's in pencil so you can just erase anything that's wrong.
這是用鉛筆寫的，這樣你就可以把任何錯誤的地方擦掉。
A virus erased my hard disk.
病毒把我硬碟中的資訊給刪了。
He is determined to erase the memory of a disappointing debut two years ago.
他決心要把兩年前初次參加比賽時令人失望的表現永遠忘掉。
Woods wants a convincing victory to erase doubts about his team's ability to reach the World Cup finals.
伍茲想要透過大比數獲勝來消除人們對他的球隊能否打入世界盃決賽的疑慮。
One election cannot erase 65 years of a corrupt one-party political process.
一場選舉並不能將長達65年腐敗的一黨專政的政治歷程抹去。
The president said NATO expansion would finally erase the boundary line in Europe artificially created by the Cold War.
總統說北約的擴展將最終消除冷戰在歐洲造成的人為界限。
Years of hard living had blurred but not erased her girlhood beauty.
多年的艱辛歲月使她芳容暗淡，但少女時代的美貌仍然依稀可辨。
He was a man of mystery - erased from the history books.
他是一個充滿神秘色彩的人物——有關他的任何情況都已不見於史冊。
